issues.description: The conceptual roles and ordering of arguments for correct_teleportation are inconsistent between the problem description/template and the solution usage. The function is documented/signatured to accept (teleportation_measurements, x_measurements) but in the solution it is invoked with the X-basis measurements as the first argument and the teleportation (ancilla) measurements as the second argument. This swapped ordering creates confusion for students implementing the function (they may follow the docstring/signature but see the opposite ordering used in the reference run), and could lead to incorrect wiring of corrections in their solutions.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the intended argument order explicit and consistent in all artifacts. Either (a) update the function signature/docstring to state explicitly that the first argument is X-basis measurements and the second is teleportation measurements, and adjust the template/tests accordingly; or (b) keep the documented order (teleportation_measurements, x_measurements) and change all call sites in the solution (and any example code) to pass measurements[:, tele] then measurements[:, final]. Ensure the docstring, template stub, and all usages match exactly so students can implement without ambiguity.
